name: Manoah and his wife
charge: Asking how shall we order the child, and doing all that was commanded them
summary: The angel of the Lord appeared to a barren woman of Zorah and told her she would bear a son who was to be a Nazarite from the womb, and gave her a rule for herself as well. She told her husband. He entreated the Lord that the man of God might come again and teach them what they should do unto the child, and the angel came again to the woman in the field, and she ran for her husband. They offered a kid on a rock and the angel ascended in the flame.
offense: Israel had again done evil and had been delivered into the Philistines' hand for forty years when the angel appeared to Manoah's barren wife (Judges 13:1-3). The promise of a son was also the beginning of an answer to the nation's affliction. The child would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines, and his dedication would start in the womb (Judges 13:5). The mother was commanded to drink no wine or strong drink and eat no unclean thing. No razor was to come upon the child's head (Judges 13:4-7). Numbers 6:1-5 gives the separation of the Nazarite: abstinence from the vine and uncut hair during the vow. Nazarite describes consecration, not residence in Nazareth. The instructions were particular, and the promise did not release the household from observing them. Manoah prayed for the messenger to return and teach them how to order the child. When the angel came again, he repeated what had already been commanded to the woman (Judges 13:8-14). Their task was not to invent a manner of upbringing because the child was extraordinary. They were to receive and keep the instruction given. The Lord's purpose for a child lays responsibility upon those raising him. When Manoah offered hospitality, the angel directed any burnt offering to the Lord, not to himself (Judges 13:15-16). Colossians 2:18 warns against worshipping angels, and the angel before John likewise commanded him to worship God (Revelation 22:8-9). Honour toward a heavenly messenger must not become the worship that belongs to the one who sent him.
judgment: Manoah offered the kid and meat offering to the Lord upon a rock. The angel ascended in the flame, and the husband and wife fell upon their faces (Judges 13:19-20). They had received a heavenly visitation, but they had not seen the Most High himself. The messenger's appearance and departure made clear that the promise was no ordinary man's assurance. Manoah feared they would die. His wife answered from what the Lord had done: he had accepted their offering, shown them these things, and announced what was to come (Judges 13:21-23). She weighed the fear against the received promise. The Lord had instructed them concerning a child's life, not prepared them for their own immediate destruction. She bore Samson; he grew, the Lord blessed him, and the Spirit began to move him (Judges 13:24-25). Psalms 113:9 speaks of the barren woman made a joyful mother. Here the blessing reached beyond the household: the promised child would begin the deliverance of an afflicted people. The parents' part was to honour the giver by obeying what he had commanded.

verses.text: And there was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and bare not.
And the angel of the Lord appeared unto the woman, and said unto her, Behold now, thou art barren, and bearest not: but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son.
Now therefore beware, I pray thee, and drink not wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing:

For, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.
Then Manoah intreated the Lord, and said, O my Lord, let the man of God which thou didst send come again unto us, and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born.
And God hearkened to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field: but Manoah her husband was not with her.
And the woman made haste, and ran, and shewed her husband, and said unto him, Behold, the man hath appeared unto me, that came unto me the other day.
And Manoah arose, and went after his wife, and came to the man, and said unto him, Art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? And he said, I am.
And Manoah said, Now let thy words come to pass. How shall we order the child, and how shall we do unto him?
And the angel of the Lord said unto Manoah, Of all that I said unto the woman let her beware.
She may not eat of any thing that cometh of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing: all that I commanded her let her observe.

entries.commentary: The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years. This is the pattern of the book of Judges: after Joshua's death Israel went off, and nation after nation was given power over them before the great captivities ever came.
There was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. He was married, but his wife was barren; she was not able to have any children.

The angel of the Lord appeared unto the woman and told her plainly: you are barren now, but you shall conceive and bear a son, a man child. This is one of many examples in the Bible of our foremothers going through barrenness, and when the Most High was ready he enabled them to conceive. Sisters who have tried for years without children should in patience possess their souls, take comfort of the scriptures, meditate on the foremothers, and believe what the Bible says.

The angel commanded the mother herself to drink no wine nor strong drink and to eat no unclean thing, because the child would be a Nazarite unto God from the womb; even in the womb he was to be kept pure. No razor was to come on his head, for the child would be a Nazarite unto God from the womb, and he would begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines. This is one of the first examples in scripture of somebody actually living the vow that was laid out in [Numbers 6](/bible/numbers/6). Understand the difference between a Nazarite and a Nazarene. Christ was a Nazarene because he was from the city of Nazareth, not a Nazarite; he drank wine, and Nazarites could not drink the blood of the grape at all. The locks of the Nazarite also witness to who Israel is; the hair of Israel naturally grows into locks.

The woman came and told her husband that a man of God came unto her whose countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible. In verse 3 the scripture says it was the angel of the Lord, but he did not tell her, so she was not sure; she only knew his face was terrible like an angel's. The popular pictures of angels as cute babies with smooth cheeks and little white wings do not match the biblical descriptions at all. To see an angel of the Most High was a terrifying sight, not something to jump for joy about. She repeated the message: the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death, and she was to drink no wine nor strong drink nor eat any unclean thing.

Manoah entreated the Lord: let the man of God which thou didst send come again unto us and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born. The Most High hearkened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field; she made haste and ran and showed her husband that the man was back.

Manoah arose and went after his wife, came to the man, and asked, art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? He said, I am. Manoah asked how they should order the child and what they should do unto him, and the angel reiterated the instructions he had already given: of all that I said unto the woman let her beware, and all that I commanded her let her observe while she carries this son.

Manoah tried to detain the angel and make ready a kid for him, but the angel refused: though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread, and if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the Lord. The angel knew Manoah might try to offer it up to him, since he appeared like a god, so he directed the offering to the Lord. Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God because we cannot see the Most High, which is why the scriptures warn against the worshipping of angels. Manoah still did not know that he was an angel of the Lord.

Manoah asked the angel his name, so that when his sayings came to pass they might do him honour. The angel answered, why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is secret? His name was too wonderful to be uttered to him.

Manoah took a kid with a meat offering and offered it upon a rock unto the Lord, and the angel did wondrously: when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame and went out of their sight. Manoah and his wife fell on their faces to the ground at the sight. This is the kind of thing Israel was able to see and witness with their own eyes. The angel appeared no more, and then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the Lord.

Manoah said to his wife, we shall surely die, because we have seen God. This is a passage the contradictors point to, since the Bible says no man hath seen God; but God here is Elohim, which is plural and speaks of heavenly beings. They saw an angel, not the Most High God. No flesh can look upon the Most High God; he is far too fierce and terrible. The furthest anybody got was Moses seeing his back parts. His wife reasoned rightly: if the Lord were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands, neither would he have shewed us all these things.

The woman bare a son and called his name Samson, and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him. The spirit of the Lord began to move him at times in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol; the Most High began to deal with him.
